losses | | 10,000 to 40,000 killed | ~100 killed | **_La Matanza_** ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") for 'The Massacre') refers to a [communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism "Communism")\-[Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") rebellion that took place in [El Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Salvador "El Salvador") between 22 and 25 January 1932. After the revolt was suppressed, it was followed by large-scale government killings in western El Salvador, which resulted in the deaths of 10,000 to 40,000 people. Another 100 soldiers were killed during the suppression of the revolt. On 22 January 1932, members of the [Communist Party of El Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_El_Salvador "Communist Party of El Salvador") (PCES) and [Pipil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipil_people "Pipil people") peasants launched a rebellion against the [Salvadoran military government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_dictatorship_in_El_Salvador "Military dictatorship in El Salvador") due to widespread social unrest and the suppression of democratic political freedoms, especially after the cancellation of the results of the [1932 legislative election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1932_Salvadoran_legislative_election "1932 Salvadoran legislative election"). During the rebellion, the communist and Indigenous rebels, led by [Farabundo Martí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farabundo_Mart%C3%AD "Farabundo Martí") and [Feliciano Ama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feliciano_Ama "Feliciano Ama"), respectively, captured several towns and cities across western El Salvador, killing an estimated 2,000 people and causing over [US](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")$100,000 in property damage. The Salvadoran government, led by General [Maximiliano Hernández Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximiliano_Hern%C3%A1ndez_Mart%C3%ADnez "Maximiliano Hernández Martínez"), who had assumed power following the [1931 Salvadoran coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1931_Salvadoran_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat "1931 Salvadoran coup d'état"), declared [martial law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law "Martial law"), and ordered the suppression of the revolt. Most of the people who were killed during _La Matanza_, which has been described as an [ethnocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnocide "Ethnocide"), were Pipil peasants and non-combatants, causing the extermination of the majority of the [Pipil-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipil_language "Pipil language") population, which led to a near total loss of the spoken language in El Salvador. Many of the rebellion's leaders, including Martí and Ama, were executed by the military. The government's repression also forced several communist leaders to flee the country and go into exile. [![Image 18](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/98/Farabundomarti.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Farabundomarti.jpg) [Farabundo Martí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farabundo_Mart%C3%AD "Farabundo Martí") in 1929 [Social unrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_disorder "Civil disorder") in [El Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Salvador "El Salvador") began to grow in the 1920s. El Salvador had three distinct [social classes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_class "Social class"): the upper class, made up of wealthy landowners; the middle class, composed of politicians and soldiers; and the lower class, which was composed of mostly [peasants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peasant "Peasant") and workers.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFAES2007-1) In 1920, a group of [communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism "Communism") and [socialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialism "Socialism") students, teachers, and artisans, established the [Regional Federation of Salvadoran Workers](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Regional_Federation_of_Salvadoran_Workers&action=edit&redlink=1 "Regional Federation of Salvadoran Workers (page does not exist)") (FRTS), El Salvador's first [trade union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_union "Trade union") to organize rural and urban workers.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeverly198258-2) One of the rural leaders of the FRTS was [Farabundo Martí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farabundo_Mart%C3%AD "Farabundo Martí"), who, together with [Miguel Mármol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_M%C3%A1rmol "Miguel Mármol"), founded the [Communist Party of El Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_El_Salvador "Communist Party of El Salvador") (PCES) in 1930.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeverly198259-3) Between 1928 and 1932, Martí fought alongside [Augusto César Sandino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augusto_C%C3%A9sar_Sandino "Augusto César Sandino") in [Nicaragua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicaragua "Nicaragua") against the [United States' occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_occupation_of_Nicaragua "United States occupation of Nicaragua") of the country.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeverly198258-2) [![Image 19](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Drying_coffee_on_a_plantation_in_El_Salvador%28GN03500%29.jpg/250px-Drying_coffee_on_a_plantation_in_El_Salvador%28GN03500%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Drying_coffee_on_a_plantation_in_El_Salvador/(GN03500/).jpg) Drying coffee on a Salvadoran plantation in 1905 In the late-19th and early-20th centuries, the [Salvadoran economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_El_Salvador "Economy of El Salvador") was heavily dependent on exporting [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee") and [coffee beans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_bean "Coffee bean"), which accounted for 75 to 95 percent of all of El Salvador's exports by 1929. Most of the coffee plantations, and the profits made by the plantations, were owned by the so-called "[Fourteen Families](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteen_Families "Fourteen Families")".[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeverly198255-4) Due to the collapse of coffee prices worldwide as a result of the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression") in 1929, coffee producers were unable to cover the cost of producing coffee or pay their workers, leading to various coffee plantations failing and many workers to go [unemployed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment "Unemployment").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeverly198259-3) As a result of the reduced exports, national income fell 50 percent from the year prior, decreasing from US40–50¢ per day to only US20¢ per day.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFAES2007-1) ### Political situation \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=La_Matanza&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Political situation")\] #### Meléndez–Quiñónez dynasty and the 1931 election \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=La_Matanza&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Meléndez–Quiñónez dynasty and the 1931 election")\] On 9 February 1913, Salvadoran President [Manuel Enrique Araujo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Enrique_Araujo "Manuel Enrique Araujo") died to his wounds after being attacked by three farmers with [machetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machete "Machete") in [San Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Salvador "San Salvador") during an [assassination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination "Assassination") attempt.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKuny_Mena2003-5) After Araujo's death, he was succeeded by a [political dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_family "Political family"); Araujo's [vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_El_Salvador "Vice President of El Salvador"), [Carlos Meléndez Ramírez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Mel%C3%A9ndez_/(politician/) "Carlos Meléndez (politician)"), his younger brother, [Jorge Meléndez Ramírez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Mel%C3%A9ndez "Jorge Meléndez"), and their brother-in-law, [Alfonso Quiñónez Molina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_Qui%C3%B1%C3%B3nez_Molina "Alfonso Quiñónez Molina"), held the [presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_El_Salvador "President of El Salvador") of El Salvador from 1913 until 1927 in the so-called "Meléndez–Quiñónez dynasty".[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200779-6)[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-Mel%C3%A9ndez%E2%80%93Qui%C3%B1%C3%B3nez_dynasty-10) The political dynasty ended when Quiñónez Molina chose [Pío Romero Bosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%C3%ADo_Romero_Bosque "Pío Romero Bosque") as his successor, as there were no other family members who were willing to assume the presidency.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200779-6) During his term, Romero Bosque lifted restrictions on the existence of political parties in opposition to the ruling [National Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Party_/(El_Salvador/) "National Democratic Party (El Salvador)") (PDN).[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200779%E2%80%9380-11) In 1931, a [presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1931_Salvadoran_presidential_election "1931 Salvadoran presidential election") was held in the country, which is considered by historians to be the first free and fair election in Salvadoran history.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971152-12)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197141-13) The three primary candidates in the election were [Alberto Gómez Zárate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_G%C3%B3mez_Z%C3%A1rate "Alberto Gómez Zárate"), the [minister of national defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_National_Defense_of_El_Salvador "Minister of National Defense of El Salvador") during Romero Bosque's presidency,[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFAESc._2017-14) [Arturo Araujo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arturo_Araujo "Arturo Araujo"), an engineer and coffee planter who was a distant relative of Manuel Enrique Araujo, and [Maximiliano Hernández Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximiliano_Hern%C3%A1ndez_Mart%C3%ADnez "Maximiliano Hernández Martínez"), a military officer.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971152%E2%80%93153-15) Araujo and Hernández Martínez eventually ran together on a joint ticket and defeated Gómez Zárate, although they did not attain a majority of the vote.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971153-16)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197147-17) Despite the [military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_El_Salvador "Armed Forces of El Salvador")'s support for Gómez Zárate and belief that they would reject the results of the election, the armed forces upheld them.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971153-16) The Communist Party of El Salvador won several municipal elections.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeverly198259-3) #### Military coup and the canceled 1932 election \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=La_Matanza&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Military coup and the canceled 1932 election")\] [![Image 20](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/General_Maximiliano_Hern%C3%A1ndez_Mart%C3%ADnez%2C_President_of_El_Salvador.jpg/250px-General_Maximiliano_Hern%C3%A1ndez_Mart%C3%ADnez%2C_President_of_El_Salvador.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:General_Maximiliano_Hern%C3%A1ndez_Mart%C3%ADnez,_President_of_El_Salvador.jpg) General [Maximiliano Hernández Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximiliano_Hern%C3%A1ndez_Mart%C3%ADnez "Maximiliano Hernández Martínez") During Araujo's administration, El Salvador was still struggling economically as a result of the Great Depression leading to social unrest across the country.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971154-18) In an attempt to improve the economy, Araujo reduced the military's budget and ordered some military officials to retire.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971154%E2%80%93155-19) His efforts were strongly opposed by the military, which staged a [coup on 2 December 1931](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1931_Salvadoran_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat "1931 Salvadoran coup d'état"), deposing Araujo and establishing the [Civic Directory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civic_Directory "Civic Directory").[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971154%E2%80%93155-19)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200780%E2%80%9381-20)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197159%E2%80%9360-21) The military government was dissolved two days later when Hernández Martínez was declared as the country's acting president, however, his government was not recognized by the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971155%E2%80%93156,_158-22)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200781-23) The December 1931 coup began a period of [forty-eight years of military rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_dictatorship_in_El_Salvador "Military dictatorship in El Salvador") in the country.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBosch19996%E2%80%938-24) In the few days after the coup, the Communist Party of El Salvador was "cautiously optimistic" about the coup, writing an [open letter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_letter "Open letter") to Hernández Martínez's government through its _Estrella Roja_ newspaper, stating that the coup was "heroic and necessary" while also believing that his government would reimpose an exploitative capitalist system.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197180%E2%80%9381-25) Before Araujo was deposed, [municipal and legislative elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1932_Salvadoran_legislative_election "1932 Salvadoran legislative election") were scheduled for 15 December 1931, but after his government was overthrown, the military rescheduled the municipal elections for 3–5 January 1932 and the legislative elections for 10–12 January 1932.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197188-26) When the communist party began to win several municipal elections in western El Salvador, the government canceled the results of all of the municipal elections.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197189-27) The legislative elections proceeded on 10 January, and despite early polling returns indicating a communist victory in [San Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Salvador_Department "San Salvador Department"), a delayed official result announced that three non-communists won the three seats of the San Salvador department.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197191-28) Violence occurred throughout the electoral process, and at least thirty communists were killed in [Ahuachapán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahuachap%C3%A1n "Ahuachapán").[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197191-28) Preparations for revolt ----------------------- \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=La_Matanza&action=edit§ion=7 "Edit section: Preparations for revolt")\] ### Planning and attempt for compromise \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=La_Matanza&action=edit§ion=8 "Edit section: Planning and attempt for compromise")\] Due to the result of the elections, communist party leaders believed that they could no longer come to power through legal means, as Hernández Martínez's government effectively canceled the elections.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197181-29) The Communist Party of El Salvador was led by Martí and Mármol. Other communist leaders included Mario Zapata, Alfonso Luna, Rafael Bondanza, and Ismael Hernández.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197184-30) Hernández, who was a member of the [International Red Aid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Red_Aid "International Red Aid"), believed that the United States would support the rebels and mistake it as a pro-Araujo counterrevolution.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197192-31) The communists' primary inspiration for revolution was the [Bolsheviks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolsheviks "Bolsheviks")' 1917 [October Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_Revolution "October Revolution").[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197184-30) According to Abel Cuenca, a Salvadoran communist and participant in the rebellion, the rebellion was not planned until after the municipal election results were canceled, with actual planning beginning on 9 or 10 January 1932.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197186-32) In contrast, according to Jorge Schlesinger, a Salvadoran writer, Martí began planning the rebellion in mid-December 1931 while in [Puerto Cortés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Cort%C3%A9s "Puerto Cortés"), [Honduras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honduras "Honduras"). His claim, however, has been essentially discredited as his piece of evidence for his claim, a letter allegedly written by Martí discussing the rebellion, was dated to 16 December 1932, rather than 1931.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197187-33) In a final attempt to avoid a violent rebellion, the communist party sent a political commission consisting of Zapata, Luna, Clemente Abel Estrada, Rubén Darío Fernández, and Joaquín Rivas to the [National Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Palace_/(El_Salvador/) "National Palace (El Salvador)") to enter into negotiations with the government. The commission was not allowed to meet directly with Hernández Martínez, instead being directed to Colonel [Joaquín Valdés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joaqu%C3%ADn_Vald%C3%A9s "Joaquín Valdés"), the minister of national defense,[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFAESc._2017-14) where the commission demanded "substantial contributions to the welfare of the peasants" in exchange for a cessation of illegal activities, threatening to revolt if the demands were not met.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197191-28) Reportedly, Luna told Valdés, "the peasants will win with their machetes the [rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights "Human rights") you are denying them", to which Valdés responded, "you have machetes; we have [machine guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_gun "Machine gun")". The meeting ended with no [compromise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compromise "Compromise") being met.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197192-31) ### Government knowledge of the rebellion \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=La_Matanza&action=edit§ion=9 "Edit section: Government knowledge of the rebellion")\] Just before the rebellion, [Juan Pablo Wainwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Pablo_Wainwright "Juan Pablo Wainwright") was arrested in [Guatemala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala "Guatemala"). Wainwright was a communist party member who was rallying support from communists in Guatemala to invade El Salvador to overthrow Hernández Martínez's government, and his arrest ended the possibility of a foreign invasion force from aiding rebels in El Salvador.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197192-31) On 18 January, Martí, Luna, and Zapata were arrested by the Salvadoran government,[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUCSDc._2020-34) but the arrests were not made public until 20 January, and plans to attack the barracks in San Salvador were captured by the army.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197193-35) On 21 January, the government instructed newspapers in the country to report that a rebellion was planned to occur the following day.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197194-36) Cuenca theorized that Hernández Martínez intentionally allowed the revolt to happen by preventing the opportunity for social and political reform to occur. The theory asserts that the intention of letting revolution occur was to crush it forcibly, as he believed the movement was doomed to fail, and that the suppression of the communist uprising would help him gain support and recognition from the United States.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197184%E2%80%9385-37) Dr. Alejandro D. Marroquín argued that Hernández Martínez actually feared a potential attack from Araujo's [Labor Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_Party_/(El_Salvador/) "Labor Party (El Salvador)") from Guatemala, rather than the communist rebellion itself. He argued that Hernández Martínez allowed the rebellion to occur and crushed it by force to deprive Araujo of an armed movement to help bring him back to power.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197185%E2%80%9386-38) [![Image 21](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Machete_Bolo.JPG/250px-Machete_Bolo.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Machete_Bolo.JPG) [Machetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machete "Machete") were one of the primary weapons used by the peasant rebels. In the late hours of 22 January 1932, thousands of peasants in the western part of the country, armed with sticks, machetes, and "poor-quality" [shotguns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun "Shotgun"), rose up in rebellion against Hernández Martínez's regime.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200728-39)[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChing1998205%E2%80%93206-40) According to General José Tomás Calderón, an estimated 70,000 to 80,000 rebels were involved in the uprising.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKeogh198213-41) Rebels led by [Francisco Sánchez](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Francisco_S%C3%A1nchez_\(Salvadoran_revolutionary\)&action=edit&redlink=1 "Francisco Sánchez (Salvadoran revolutionary) (page does not exist)") ([es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_%22Chico%22_S%C3%A1nchez "es:Francisco \"Chico\" Sánchez")) attacked telegraph offices, their primary target, in [Juayúa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juay%C3%BAa "Juayúa") at 11:00 p.m. and eventually took control of the city due to a lack of a military presence.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFAES2007-1)[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197198%E2%80%9399-42) The rebels attacked the home of Emilio Radaelli, a coffee merchant referred to as the "richest man in town",[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200729%E2%80%9330-43) and assassinated him, along with his son and wife, who was also raped.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFAES2007-1)[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200730-44) Radaelli's house and two of his stores were burned, with many more stores being looted.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200730-44) Colonel Mateo Vaquero was also killed by the rebels and several civilians were tortured and murdered.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFAES2007-1) Miguel Call, the mayor of [Izalco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Izalco "Izalco"), Rafael Castro Cármaco, a politician from [Chalchuapa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalchuapa "Chalchuapa"), and General Rafael Rivas, the military commander of [Tacuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tacuba "Tacuba"), were also killed by the rebels.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200729,_32-45) > "After invading the town, they \[the rebels\] set fire to the municipal building, destroying it completely, and then proceeded to break down the doors of the homes of Señor Antonio Salaverría, Dr. Tiburico Morán, Señorita Rosenda Rodríguez, don Benjamín Inocente Orantes, don Moisés Canales, don Francisco Pérez Alvarado, and the local bar. In the home of José Dolores Salaverría they broke the windows above a balcony. In the aforementioned houses, in addition to inflicting serious structural damage, the rebels destroyed all sorts of furniture and objects of value." M. Figueroa, military commander of Salcoatitán, 14 March 1932[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200731-46) Businesses and homes were destroyed by rebels, with the total property damage inflicted being estimated at around [SVC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvadoran_col%C3%B3n "Salvadoran colón")₡300,000 (approximately [US](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")$120,000 in 1932). Much of the damage was inflicted against property owned by wealthy individuals and families.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200731-46) Eventually, the rebels captured the towns of [Colón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col%C3%B3n,_La_Libertad "Colón, La Libertad"), Juayúa, [Nahuizalco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahuizalco "Nahuizalco"), [Salcoatitán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salcoatit%C3%A1n "Salcoatitán"), [Sonzacate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonzacate "Sonzacate"), and Tacuba.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200729-47) Additionally, [Pipil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipil_people "Pipil people") rebels led by [Feliciano Ama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feliciano_Ama "Feliciano Ama") supported the communist rebels and captured the town of Izalco on 23 January.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200732-48) Ama was an influential Indigenous leader in Izalco, and believed that joining the rebellion would help him gain political office. Meanwhile, the majority of the Pipil rebels were sympathetic to the communists' ideals, and believed that they possessed a "secret weapon or magic" which would assure victory.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197169%E2%80%9370-49) Despite efforts to prevent communication with the military garrisons in [Ahuachapán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahuachap%C3%A1n "Ahuachapán"), [Sonsonate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonsonate,_El_Salvador "Sonsonate, El Salvador"), and [Santa Ana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Ana,_El_Salvador "Santa Ana, El Salvador"), Izalco managed to send a telegram to Sonsonate warning the military garrison there of the rebel attacks before the telegraph office was destroyed.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200732-48) The warning was received by the military garrison in Sonsonate, and in response, Colonel Ernesto Bará sent an expeditionary force under the command of Major Mariano Molina to crush the rebellion on 23 January. Molina's soldiers first clashed with the rebels outside of Sonzacate, and after engaging in hand-to-hand combat, the rebels retreated to the city proper.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200732%E2%80%9333-50) Casualties from the battle included fifty to seventy dead rebels, five dead soldiers, and half a dozen more soldiers wounded.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200733-51) The Canadian warships [HMCS _Skeena_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMCS_Skeena_/(D59/) "HMCS Skeena (D59)") and [HMCS _Vancouver_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMCS_Vancouver_/(F6A/) "HMCS Vancouver (F6A)") were docked at the Port of [Acajutla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acajutla "Acajutla"), and the ships were requested by the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") to protect any British citizens in the country. Ships from the United States arrived shortly after and the ships offered to assist the Salvadoran government in quelling the rebellion,[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200740-52) however, Calderón turned down the offer, stating: > The chief of Operation of the Western Zone of the Republic, Major General José Tomás Calderón, presents his compliments on behalf of the government of General Martínez and of himself, to Admiral Smith and Commander Brandeur, of the [Rochester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_New_York_/(ACR-2/) "USS New York (ACR-2)"), Skeena, and Vancouver, I am pleased to announce that peace in El Salvador is restored, that the communist offensive has been completely suppressed and dispersed, and that complete extermination will be achieved. 4,800 Bolsheviks were wiped out.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUES1995-53) — José Tomás Calderón On 23 January, Hernández Martínez published a manifesto in the _[Diario Oficial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Press_of_El_Salvador "National Press of El Salvador")_, the official national newspaper of El Salvador. The manifesto read: [![Image 22](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Manifiesto_mhm.jpg/250px-Manifiesto_mhm.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manifiesto_mhm.jpg) Maximiliano Hernández Martínez's manifesto regarding the uprising > Fellow citizens: > > The Republic of El Salvador, profoundly agitated by the social problems and the acute economic crisis, traverses the most difficult hours of its independent life. In the last few days, the Government has seen grave events of communist origin and, with foundation in the national laws, I have had the impressionable necessity to suffocate them with a strong hand. Executive guidelines, charged with ensuring tranquility and the wellbeing of Salvadorans, are and will be severely punished for any alteration of public order and any act that attacks the social structure and the rights to property, liberty, and life of the inhabitants. > > The Government makes a call to the sanity and patriotism of the citizens to the effect that in these difficult circumstances, everyone, in the sphere of its activities, surround and support the Executive so that peace is not altered. We wish that the different social classes, friends of the order, know how to respond to this appeal, in a practical and decided form, now that against them raises the communist activities. > > The Government counts on the loyalty of the Army and the public security forces, and has the firm purpose to now allow, under any concept, the minor action of the disruptive hordes. The Salvadoran people can have certainty that the Government has the capacity to strongly reap every revolutionary outbreak; but expect for them the unanimous and effective cooperation of all the social classes, in these grave and haunting moments for the future of the fatherland. > > The current political regime inspires and continues to inspire the sane intention of giving the country the largest margin of liberties, and maintain order, labor, and the capacity of all governmental forces, so that the nation channels its march of progress through new channels, and the inhabitants can tranquilly dedicate themselves to labor and all the honest and constructive activities. > > Because of that, the Government laments the shedding of blood and the restriction of liberties, which was seen as obligated to decree to suppress the vandalous communist activities; but have faith that once the Salvadoran people forms a single bloc of defense with the Government, peace, constitutional order, and the state of liberty will return to restore itself, guaranteed by the emancipatory political ideology that informs the men of the present Government. > > Fellow citizens: The Chief of the Executive has plenty faith in that the Salvadorans, in this hour of test, in which the homeland, the property, and the lives of all the inhabitants which are found threatened, will know how to defend with integrity the expensive and vital interests of the fatherland.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHern%C3%A1ndez_Mart%C3%ADnez1932-54) — Maximiliano Hernández Martínez Quickly after the uprising in 24 January 1932, the government declared [martial law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law "Martial law") and mobilized the military to crush the rebellion by force.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971163-55) Soldiers under the command of Colonel Marcelino Galdámez marched into the departments of [Sonsonate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonsonate_Department "Sonsonate Department") and [Ahuachapán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahuachap%C3%A1n_Department "Ahuachapán Department") and captured Izalco that same day.[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200736-56) Nahuizalco, Salcoatitán, Juayúa were all captured the next day, and the rebellion was fully crushed by the afternoon of 25 January 1932.[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200737-57) Around 100 soldiers were killed during the rebellion's suppression.[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUCA-58) Subsequent government killings ------------------------------ \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=La_Matanza&action=edit§ion=11 "Edit section: Subsequent government killings")\] [![Image 23](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Dead_bodies_of_the_killing_of_the_salvadorean_army_in_1932.jpg/250px-Dead_bodies_of_the_killing_of_the_salvadorean_army_in_1932.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dead_bodies_of_the_killing_of_the_salvadorean_army_in_1932.jpg) Dead bodies of people killed by the army during _La Matanza_ On 25 January 1932, reinforcements under Calderón arrived in Sonsonate and began [reprisals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reprisal "Reprisal") against peasants, especially against ethnic Pipils, in western El Salvador, indiscriminately killing thousands of civilians in the process.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200737_&_62-59) In several towns, the entire male population was gathered in the town's center and killed by machine gun fire. The killings persisted for two weeks until February 1932 when the government decided that the region had been sufficiently "pacified".[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200738-60) René Padilla Velasco, Martí's lawyer during his [show trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Show_trial "Show trial"), argued that Hernández Martínez forced Martí to launch the rebellion as a final "desperate" effort to prevent him from consolidating dictatorial control of the country.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197187%E2%80%9388-61) Martí, Luna, and Zapata were [executed by a firing squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_by_firing_squad "Execution by firing squad") on 1 February 1932.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUCSDc._2020-34)[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGaleano2010110-62) Ama and Sánchez were captured by the army in Izalco on 25 January 1932; Sánchez was executed by a firing squad that same day,[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson1971126-63) while Ama was [lynched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynching "Lynching") in a plaza in the city on 28 January 1932.[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGaleano2010110-62) Many refugees attempted to flee the country to Guatemala to escape the government's repression, however, Guatemalan President [Jorge Ubico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Ubico "Jorge Ubico") closed the [border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Salvador%E2%80%93Guatemala_border "El Salvador–Guatemala border") and handed over those who tried to flee back to the Salvadoran Army.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUES1995-53) On 11 July 1932, the [Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legislative_Assembly_of_El_Salvador "Legislative Assembly of El Salvador") passed Directive 121 which officially declared an end to the rebellion. It also granted "unconditional amnesty" ("_incondicional amnistía_") to anyone—rebel, military, or otherwise—who committed crimes of any nature in order to "restore order, repress, persecute, punish, and capture those accused of the crime of rebellion" ("_restablecimiento del orden, represión, persecución, castigo y captura de los sindicados en el delito derebelión_").[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTECu%C3%A9llar_Mart%C3%ADnez20041,087-64) Estimates of the exact death toll of the rebellion and subsequent government killings vary greatly; the figures most commonly estimated are between 10,000 and 40,000 dead.[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTETulchinBland1992167-65) According to a Sonsonate resident interviewed by journalist Joaquín Méndez, the rebels killed approximately 2,000 people.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200732-48) Colonel [Osmín Aguirre y Salinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osm%C3%ADn_Aguirre_y_Salinas "Osmín Aguirre y Salinas"), the chief of the [National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Police_of_El_Salvador "National Police of El Salvador"), stated that no more than 6,000 to 7,000 people were "executed".[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson1971135-66) According to John Beverly, around 30,000 people—four percent of the population—were killed by the government.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeverly198259-3) As a result of the large scale of the killings, the event has since been referred to as _La Matanza_ ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") for "The Massacre").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeverly198259-3)[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBosch19997-67) Following the mass killings, Hernández Martínez solidified his rule when the legislature confirmed his presidency in 1932. He also sought to legitimize his rule via presidential elections in [1935](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935_Salvadoran_presidential_election "1935 Salvadoran presidential election"), [1939](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1939_Salvadoran_presidential_election "1939 Salvadoran presidential election"), and [1944](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1944_Salvadoran_presidential_election "1944 Salvadoran presidential election"), in which he was the only candidate.[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaggerty199017%E2%80%9318-68) He exercised control of the country through force via the army and through friendly relations with the country's landowners and elites.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBosch19998-69) Hernández Martínez was the country's longest serving [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_El_Salvador "President of El Salvador"), serving from 1931 to 1944 when he resigned following an [attempted coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Sunday_Coup "Palm Sunday Coup") and a series of [mass protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_of_Fallen_Arms "Strike of Fallen Arms") against his government.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaggerty199018-70)[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBosch19998-69) Hernández Martínez's government was not recognized by the United States after it came to power in 1931 due to the [1923 Central American Treaty of Peace and Amity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1923_Central_American_Treaty_of_Peace_and_Amity "1923 Central American Treaty of Peace and Amity") which mandates its signatories shall not recognize any government which came to power via a coup d'état.[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971159%E2%80%93160-71) Mauricio de la Selva, a Salvadoran poet and communist writer, theorized that Hernández Martínez crushed the rebellion with such violence as to appear to the United States as a "champion of [anti-communism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-communism "Anti-communism")".[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson197185-72) The United States did eventually recognize Hernández Martínez's regime on 26 January 1934, not because of his government's anti-communist ideology, but because the United States perceived his government as bringing stability to the country.[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrieb1971170-73)[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200782-74) [![Image 24](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Bandera_-_Frente_Farabundo_Mart%C3%AD_para_la_Liberaci%C3%B3n_Nacional.svg/250px-Bandera_-_Frente_Farabundo_Mart%C3%AD_para_la_Liberaci%C3%B3n_Nacional.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bandera_-_Frente_Farabundo_Mart%C3%AD_para_la_Liberaci%C3%B3n_Nacional.svg) The [FMLN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farabundo_Mart%C3%AD_National_Liberation_Front "Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front") was named after Farabundo Martí, one of the rebellion's leaders. Most of the surviving leaders of the Communist Party of El Salvador fled the country, primarily to [Honduras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honduras "Honduras") and [Costa Rica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costa_Rica "Costa Rica").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeverly198259-3) The communist party itself was not banned, and it remained active in El Salvador throughout Hernández Martínez's presidency. The party even supported the mass protests which led to Hernández Martínez's resignation in 1944.[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez2007194%E2%80%93197-75) In 1980, various left-wing militia groups of the [Salvadoran Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvadoran_Civil_War "Salvadoran Civil War") joined forces and formed the [Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farabundo_Mart%C3%AD_National_Liberation_Front "Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front") (FMLN), named after Martí.[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez2007184_&_242-76) The FMLN continues to exist as one of El Salvador's major political parties.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez2007245-77) ### Effect on Indigenous communities \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=La_Matanza&action=edit§ion=15 "Edit section: Effect on Indigenous communities")\] Some scholars label the mass killings of Pipil as an [ethnocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnocide "Ethnocide"),[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTECISPES2007-78)[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPay%C3%A9s2007-79) since the army used Indigenous appearance, dress, and language to help designate who should be targeted.[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindo_FuentesChingLara_Mart%C3%ADnez200762-80) As a result, in the decades that followed, Salvadoran Indigenous peoples increasingly abandoned their native dress and traditional languages for fear of further reprisals.[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPBSc._2002-81)[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGarrard-Burnett2004575%E2%80%93576-82)[\[82\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEde_la_Rosa_Municio2006-83) The events brought about the extermination of the majority of the [Pipil-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipil_language "Pipil language") population, which led to a near total loss of the spoken language in El Salvador.[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEde_Maeztu1932-84)[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTESuateac._2004-85) Many of the Indigenous people who did not participate in the uprising stated that they did not understand the motivation of the government's persecution.[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTETerra_El_Salvadorc._2007-86) Over the years since _La Matanza_, the recorded population willing to self-identify as Indigenous has fallen to about 10 percent in the 21st century. In the decade following the uprising, military presence in the area was persistent with the objective of keeping the peasants under control so that the events did not recur. After the dictatorship of Hernández Martínez, the method of preventing peasant discontent changed from repression to social reforms which benefitted them.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKohanc._2007-87)[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEICARRDc._2006-88) In the town of Izalco, the uprising is commemorated annually on 22 January. Media coverage is moderate, but the commemoration is supported by municipal authorities who pay tribute to all who were killed during the event. Speakers include people who lived through the event, and relatives of Ama.[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPay%C3%A9s2007-79)[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGarc%C3%ADa_Due%C3%B1as2005-89) In 2010, President [Mauricio Funes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauricio_Funes "Mauricio Funes"), the first Salvadoran president to be a member of the FMLN, apologized to the Indigenous communities of El Salvador for the brutal acts of persecution and extermination carried out by previous governments. In a statement made during the inauguration of the First Congress of Indigenous Peoples, he stated, "In this context and this spirit, my government wishes to be the first government to, on behalf of the State of El Salvador, of the people of El Salvador, and of the families of El Salvador, make an act of contrition and apologize to the Indigenous communities for the persecution and extermination of which they were victims during so many years" ("_Este gobierno que presido, quiere ser el primer gobierno que en nombre del Estado salvadoreño, en nombre del pueblo salvadoreño, en nombre de las familias salvadoreñas, haga un acto de contrición y pida perdón a las comunidades indígenas, por la persecución y por el exterminio de que fueron víctimas, durante tantos y tantos años_").[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEl_Salvador_Noticias2010-90) The [Jeffrey Gould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Gould "Jeffrey Gould")\-directed 2002
